brief: A portable electronics organizer: a base with removable bins for small parts, at least one drawer, and a carry handle.

requirements.evidence: piece:0,0,0;full plus piece:0,1,0;half-n, bolted together with jointBolt:0#0,0#5. All open side faces are capped.

Two drop-in bins: bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full-div3 (three compartments) and bin:0,1,0~hex-bin-half-n-full-div3. They are separate parts that sit in the bases. The full base's bin is under the top cover, so you take the cover off to reach it. The half base's bin sits under its own top cover. Screw, nut and standoff props are staged in the full bin.
drawer:0#0,1#cut on the cut face of the half base, shown open with a pile of M3 standoffs inside.

handle:0,0,0;top is fitted on cover:0,0,0;full;top, which places it over the middle of the full cell. The configurator checks fit only, so it can't confirm that the handle and joints will hold the organizer's weight when lifted.

The organizer is a compact two-cell block with a top handle and locked joints, so its shape suits carrying. Strength and weight depend on the material you print it in, which the configurator doesn't check.

finish.summary: I built a two-cell electronics organizer. It has a full hex base and a north-half base locked together, a divided bin in each base, a pull-out drawer on the cut face of the half base and a carry handle on the full base's top cover. The build check passes with no errors and the mesh-collision check reads clear. The configurator only checks fit and collisions, so it says nothing about how much weight the handle can carry. The screws, nuts and standoffs I put in as display props sit under the lid and below the drawer rim, so they don't show in the default view.

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
